positions.name: KnowledgeExcisionDirective
positions.frame: what is the organization's posture toward knowledge that should be excised from its record?
positions.why: Two directives command the removal of all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work, while the assertive retroactively denies the observatory ever performed the calibration. Together they express a unified posture of excision — not merely forgetting but asserting the activity never occurred — read through the question of how the organization handles knowledge it determines should no longer exist.
